overview.overview:
Nebraska's statewide electoral votes are expected to go to the Republican candidate by a wide margin. The state voted Republican by about 19 points in 2020 and 20 points in 2024, and it sits roughly 20 points to the right of the nation as a whole. The forecast expects a Republican margin of about 15 points, somewhat narrower than recent results, reflecting a national environment that leans toward Democrats.

Even at the favorable end of the expected range, a Democratic win statewide would require an unusually large shift. Nebraska's two at-large electoral votes are not competitive, and the state has essentially no chance of being the tipping point in the election.
overview.watch: A sufficiently large national Democratic wave could narrow the margin further, though a statewide win remains a distant possibility.
key_factors: Nebraska's strong Republican baseline, roughly 20 points right of the nation
A national environment tilted several points toward Democrats, which narrows the expected margin
Limited statewide polling, leaving uncertainty around the exact margin
